items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented as an active problem (Condition 7010d0e5, ICD-9 427.31) and repeatedly carried in the cardiology clinic problem list (e.g. progress notes 2025-10-10, 2025-12-13, 2026-03-23, 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease from coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery, ICD-9 414.01), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. His only current outpatient order is tamsulosin (cc9e3a71, 2026-07-28); no oral anticoagulant has ever been prescribed (only a peri-procedural heparin flush in Aug 2025). Needs review for starting anticoagulation.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) first appears at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (DocumentReference 55f064b7; first outpatient citalopram order 7f7af72f on 2026-03-07). Because the start was on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) applies and required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, within the window, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (DocumentReference 93604d42; order 88da30d3 the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. No ECG was obtained in that window - the only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not recorded until 2026-04-29 (19 days after the start), outside the required time - so the requirement was not met by its due date and is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (DocumentReference fa831ef2; order d6dc36c8 the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the most recent tracing in the chart is 106035722 of 2025-12-25 - and nothing in the chart refers to an outside ECG, so the requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (DocumentReference a8e85155; order b3f9658b the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the required window - and the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside result could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (DocumentReference 33136968; order a9c255d8 the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained yet (most recent is 104253928 of 2025-03-09), but the due date falls after the 2026-09-24 review time, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily (DocumentReference b32487e8). Per the memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 372c7683) an INR was required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation 25b9e47a), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4 (DocumentReference 9579a764); the 2024-06-01 standing order (DocumentReference a82fdaa4) authorises clinic pharmacists to make such changes, so this is a qualifying dose change. Per the memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 372c7683) an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been resulted since; the requirement is therefore overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list (Condition 66dd1300, ICD-10 I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior ischaemic stroke with residual left hemiparesis (I63.9/I63.40 and sequelae I69.354/I69.392/I69.893) = 2, hypertension (I10, I12.9, 401.9) = 1, age 65-74 = 1, female sex = 1. Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended. Current outpatient orders (2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only; no anticoagulant is or has been prescribed, and the clinic notes never address AF or stroke prophylaxis. Needs review for starting anticoagulation.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is currently ordered (MedicationRequest dc397aff, authored 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28). However, the outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) documents an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 at Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note nevertheless continued apixaban (with aspirin and clopidogrel) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. The anticoagulant should not continue without prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (MedicationRequest 99b4dc24, authored 2026-07-15, valid through 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (MedicationRequest 0ba6a357, authored 2026-07-15, valid through 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note (DocumentReference a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-ordered rather than stopped and it still appears on the medication list. Overlapping factor Xa inhibitors carry a major bleeding risk; the duplicate order needs to be discontinued.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) records "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 142 and 144 bpm with no organised P waves (RR coefficient of variation 0.18 and 0.16; averaged P-wave amplitude <0.06 mV, low beat-to-beat P correlation) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, consistent with her documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 54ec94da) and with the AF rhythm entries charted 6/10-6/12/2026. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current QT watch-list order (MedicationRequest c6f532e9, authored 2026-08-22, valid through 2027-01-05; on amiodarone continuously since 2022). Her most recent ECG in the chart, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, is sinus rhythm at 58 bpm (RR 1.044 s) with QT about 560 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 547 ms - at or above the clinic threshold of 500 ms, so prescriber review is required per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15. Most recent electrolytes (both 2026-02-14) are potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL, i.e. not obviously contributory. No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continued amiodarone plus warfarin.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a current QT watch-list order (MedicationRequest f9708e2d, authored 2026-05-29, valid through 2026-12-25; citalopram continuously since 2023-10-02). Her most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, is sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 0.856 s) with QT about 510 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 551 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold, so prescriber review is required per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15. Note that 40 mg daily also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended where QT prolongation is a concern. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current QT watch-list order (MedicationRequest 1014aca9, authored 2026-07-29, valid through 2027-01-05; started 2025-11-10 for atrial fibrillation). His most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, is sinus rhythm at 62 bpm (RR 0.968 s) with QT about 527 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 536 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold, so prescriber review is required per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20) are normal. He also remains on warfarin, and no repeat ECG has been obtained since the prolonged tracing.

Amiodarone (a QT watch-list medication) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (DocumentReference aa0ab6aa; order e578297f the same day). The memo in force at that time (2025-09-01, DocumentReference e25bb79f) required an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met within the required time.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented as an active problem (Condition 7010d0e5, ICD-9 427.31) and repeatedly carried in the cardiology clinic problem list (e.g. progress notes 2025-10-10, 2025-12-13, 2026-03-23, 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease from coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery, ICD-9 414.01), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. His only current outpatient order is tamsulosin (cc9e3a71, 2026-07-28); no oral anticoagulant has ever been prescribed (only a peri-procedural heparin flush in Aug 2025). Needs review for starting anticoagulation.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) first appears at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (DocumentReference 55f064b7; first outpatient citalopram order 7f7af72f on 2026-03-07). Because the start was on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) applies and required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, within the window, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (DocumentReference 93604d42; order 88da30d3 the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. No ECG was obtained in that window - the only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not recorded until 2026-04-29 (19 days after the start), outside the required time - so the requirement was not met by its due date and is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (DocumentReference fa831ef2; order d6dc36c8 the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the most recent tracing in the chart is 106035722 of 2025-12-25 - and nothing in the chart refers to an outside ECG, so the requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (DocumentReference a8e85155; order b3f9658b the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the required window - and the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside result could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (DocumentReference 33136968; order a9c255d8 the same day). Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 2a70ec05) an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained yet (most recent is 104253928 of 2025-03-09), but the due date falls after the 2026-09-24 review time, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily (DocumentReference b32487e8). Per the memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 372c7683) an INR was required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation 25b9e47a), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met within the required time.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4 (DocumentReference 9579a764); the 2024-06-01 standing order (DocumentReference a82fdaa4) authorises clinic pharmacists to make such changes, so this is a qualifying dose change. Per the memo effective 2026-03-01 (DocumentReference 372c7683) an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been resulted since; the requirement is therefore overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list (Condition 66dd1300, ICD-10 I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior ischaemic stroke with residual left hemiparesis (I63.9/I63.40 and sequelae I69.354/I69.392/I69.893) = 2, hypertension (I10, I12.9, 401.9) = 1, age 65-74 = 1, female sex = 1. Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended. Current outpatient orders (2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only; no anticoagulant is or has been prescribed, and the clinic notes never address AF or stroke prophylaxis. Needs review for starting anticoagulation.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is currently ordered (MedicationRequest dc397aff, authored 2026-08-20, valid through 2026-12-28). However, the outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) documents an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 at Mercy Hospital for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note nevertheless continued apixaban (with aspirin and clopidogrel) without any documented reassessment of the bleed. The anticoagulant should not continue without prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (MedicationRequest 99b4dc24, authored 2026-07-15, valid through 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (MedicationRequest 0ba6a357, authored 2026-07-15, valid through 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note (DocumentReference a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-ordered rather than stopped and it still appears on the medication list. Overlapping factor Xa inhibitors carry a major bleeding risk; the duplicate order needs to be discontinued.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) records "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 142 and 144 bpm with no organised P waves (RR coefficient of variation 0.18 and 0.16; averaged P-wave amplitude <0.06 mV, low beat-to-beat P correlation) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, consistent with her documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 54ec94da) and with the AF rhythm entries charted 6/10-6/12/2026. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current QT watch-list order (MedicationRequest c6f532e9, authored 2026-08-22, valid through 2027-01-05; on amiodarone continuously since 2022). Her most recent ECG in the chart, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, is sinus rhythm at 58 bpm (RR 1.044 s) with QT about 560 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 547 ms - at or above the clinic threshold of 500 ms, so prescriber review is required per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15. Most recent electrolytes (both 2026-02-14) are potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL, i.e. not obviously contributory. No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continued amiodarone plus warfarin.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a current QT watch-list order (MedicationRequest f9708e2d, authored 2026-05-29, valid through 2026-12-25; citalopram continuously since 2023-10-02). Her most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, is sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 0.856 s) with QT about 510 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 551 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold, so prescriber review is required per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15. Note that 40 mg daily also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended where QT prolongation is a concern. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current QT watch-list order (MedicationRequest 1014aca9, authored 2026-07-29, valid through 2027-01-05; started 2025-11-10 for atrial fibrillation). His most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, is sinus rhythm at 62 bpm (RR 0.968 s) with QT about 527 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 536 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold, so prescriber review is required per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20) are normal. He also remains on warfarin, and no repeat ECG has been obtained since the prolonged tracing.
